source.title: On The Application of Linear Attention in Multimodal Transformers
source.authors: Armin Gerami; Seyedehanita Madani; R. Duraiswami

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a power-law loss-versus-model-size pattern transfers to multimodal image-text models trained with linear attention, a new setting for the scaling-law claim.
record.gate_note: The paper measures training loss at epoch 30 and reports fits against model size. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss, token-count scaling, or compute-optimal allocation. Runtime results and ImageNet-21K zero-shot accuracy results do not test the power-law loss versions.
record.test_reason: The study fits a power law of training loss against parameter count for CLIP ViT-S/B/L on LAION-400M (Eq. 8, Fig. 4), with standard and linear attention. This is a result on whether the power-law form holds in image-text contrastive training (V5). It does not vary tokens or compute, does not extrapolate, and reports no held-out loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that modified linear attention matches standard attention's performance, gives linear runtime in sequence length, and follows a similar empirical loss–model size power-law trend.
record.recipe_differences: This is a multimodal image-text ViT study using an affine linear-attention kernel, normalized queries and keys, and an omitted denominator, trained with OpenCLIP on LAION-400M. It measures training loss at Epoch 30 against model size rather than held-out language-model loss across parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.problems: The scaling fit uses only three model sizes, spanning 22M to 304M parameters, and reports training rather than held-out loss. No uncertainty for the fitted exponents is reported. Table 1 states 304M for ViT-L-16, while Figure 4 labels it 307M.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were omitted. Runtime measurements and ImageNet-21K zero-shot accuracy plots were not included because they do not report the power-law loss relations named by the tested version.

untested.parts: Held-out loss; scaling in data or compute; ranges beyond ~22M–304M parameters; video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer.
Not tested; no language-model loss is measured.
Not tested; no extrapolation to larger runs.
Not tested; shape is not varied at fixed parameter count.
No fit of zero-shot accuracy against size or loss is reported.
Not tested; fitting choices are not varied.

missing.what: ImageNet-21K zero-shot accuracy per model size for both attention types. The authors claim this follows accuracy–model size scaling laws, but report no fit.

record.verdict_notes: The per-model global batch sizes (64, 16, 4) differ. CLIP contrastive loss falls as the number of in-batch negatives falls, so part of the loss decrease with size may be a batch-size artifact. This seriously weakens the V5 evidence. The fits use only three points and report no uncertainty. The abstract calls this 'the same scaling laws', but the exponents differ (0.362 vs 0.332).

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from fits on small runs.
Architecture changes at a fixed parameter count.
The study tests training loss scaling in multimodal image-text models, but not other modalities such as video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer; it does not test held-out loss.
No predictable scaling relation between downstream performance and model scale or pretraining loss is fitted or reported.
The study does not vary fitting choices or establish setup-dependent exponents, compute-optimal splits, or bending curves.

rows.subject: ViT-S-16, ViT-B-16, and ViT-L-16 (aggregate scaling fit)
rows.stage_stated: trained on LAION-400M; loss at Epoch 30
rows.operation_detail: Fit training loss against model parameter count across the three ViT sizes.
rows.measure: Training loss versus model parameter count
rows.note: The fit is reported as an aggregate across the three model sizes; the paper describes the training loss as decreasing with size.
rows.check: The fit covers only three points spanning about 1.1 orders of magnitude, with no goodness of fit or exponent uncertainty. The measure is training loss, not held-out loss. Global batch size falls with model size (64, 16, 4), and contrastive loss depends on the number of negatives, so the slope is confounded with batch size.

relationships.condition: CLIP ViT-S/B/L-16 (22M–304M) on LAION-400M, training loss at epoch 30, standard and modified linear attention
relationships.reason: Power-law fits with exponents -0.362 and -0.332 describe the loss decrease with size (r1, r2). The evidence is weak: three points, about one order of magnitude, training loss, and batch size confounded with size.
relationships.display_finding: Training-loss decreases fitted power laws with exponents −0.362 and −0.332, using three points over approximately one order of magnitude with batch size confounded with model size.
